consumedBy: critique.mjs (opt-in; anchors the per-dimension reasoning pass, §2.5)
purpose: Expert-authored few-shot anchors (score 0 / 2 / 4) per scoring dimension. Calibrate the critic's DESIGN-EVAL score against real critique language before it grades a new screen — the UICrit few-shot pattern (a labelled critique corpus raised GPT-4o critique quality ~55% over zero-shot in Duan et al. 2024).

provenance.method: UICrit few-shot exemplar pattern (Duan, Wu, Li et al., 'UICrit: Enhancing Automated Design Evaluation with a UI Critique Dataset', UIST 2024, arXiv:2407.08850) — a corpus of expert design critiques used as in-context few-shot anchors.
provenance.grounding: Anchor prose is written to the DESIGN-EVAL v1 rubric (../critique_rubric.md), itself grounded in Refactoring UI (Wathan & Schoger), Material Design 3, Apple HIG, Nielsen's 10 heuristics, and WCAG 2.2 AA. These are synthetic-but-representative exemplars in the UICrit style, NOT verbatim rows from the UICrit dataset (that dataset targets mobile screens and carries its own licence).
provenance.reliabilityBaselines: UIClip inter-rater alpha 0.37; UICrit critique agreement kappa ~= 0.30 — perceptual dimensions are honestly low-agreement; anchors reduce variance but do not eliminate it.

usage.how: During a Track-B critique, before scoring dimension D, read exemplars.dimensions[D].anchors. Match the observed screen to the closest anchor band (0/2/4) and interpolate (1 = between 0 and 2; 3 = between 2 and 4). Cite the anchor id you matched in the finding evidence for traceability.
usage.onePassPerDimension: Honours §2.5 reliability protocol — one dimension per reasoning pass; use only that dimension's anchors to avoid halo bleed.
usage.shadow: This pack is advisory data only. It changes NO scoring math and adds NO gate — critique.mjs computes the same weighted composite with or without it. It only sharpens the human/critic's per-dimension judgement.
usage.criticalError: Where an anchor's score is 0 AND its band is a critical-error condition, it also carries "critical": true — mirrors §2.3 (a tripped critical forces the dimension score to 0 and caps the verdict).

visual-hierarchy.question: Does the eye land on the right thing first?

anchors.band: critical-error: no focal point AND the primary CTA is visually indistinguishable from secondary controls
anchors.critique: Every control shares the same size, weight and colour, so nothing reads as the primary action — the eye has no entry point and bounces around a flat wall of equal-weight buttons.
anchors.evidence: axe heading-order/landmark/region missing (document structure flattened); primary CTA renders at the same visual weight as three secondary controls.
anchors.recommendation: Elevate ONE primary action with size + weight + colour (not size alone); demote the rest to secondary/ghost styling; add landmark regions and a correct heading order.

anchors.band: a focal point exists but secondary actions compete for attention
anchors.critique: There is a discernible primary action, but two secondary buttons carry nearly the same emphasis, splitting attention and slowing the first fixation.
anchors.evidence: Primary CTA is distinguishable but secondary controls use a saturated fill that competes; heading order present but one level skipped.
anchors.recommendation: Reduce secondary controls to outline/text style so the primary clearly wins; reserve saturated fill for the single primary action.

anchors.band: unmistakable primary action, calm de-emphasised supporting content
anchors.critique: One primary action is instantly obvious; supporting text and secondary actions are deliberately quieter, so the eye lands exactly where intended and the screen reads in a clear sequence.
anchors.evidence: Single high-emphasis CTA; secondary actions low-emphasis; correct landmark + heading hierarchy; supporting copy de-emphasised in weight and colour.
anchors.recommendation: None material — maintain the emphasis ratio as content grows.

spacing-rhythm.question: Consistent spacing scale and breathing room?

anchors.band: critical-error: content blocks overlap or collide
anchors.critique: Blocks physically overlap and text collides with adjacent elements — the layout has broken, not merely tightened.
anchors.evidence: off-scale-spacing high-confidence negative/zero gaps; overlapping bounding boxes visible in the screenshot.
anchors.recommendation: Fix the broken layout constraints first; then re-space everything onto a single 4-8px scale with clear grouping by proximity.

anchors.band: several high-confidence off-grid values, uneven rhythm
anchors.critique: Spacing is functional but arbitrary — authored values like 13px and 30px break the scale, so gutters and gaps feel uneven and slightly cramped.
anchors.evidence: off-scale-spacing high-confidence on multiple authored integers (e.g. 13, 30); inconsistent inter-card gaps.
anchors.recommendation: Snap all margins/padding/gaps to a 4-8px token scale; increase the base whitespace unit; group related items with tighter proximity than unrelated ones.

anchors.band: everything on one scale, deliberate whitespace
anchors.critique: Spacing sits on a single consistent scale with generous, even whitespace; proximity groups related items so the structure is legible before you read a word.
anchors.evidence: No high-confidence off-scale-spacing findings; only sub-pixel info-level noise; even gutters throughout.
anchors.recommendation: None material.

alignment.question: Shared edges and baselines; tidy gutters?

anchors.band: content visibly random — nothing shares an edge
anchors.critique: Elements float with no shared edges or baselines; labels, values and controls each start at a different x, so the screen looks assembled by accident.
anchors.evidence: Perceptual (no deterministic Track-A signal): ragged left edges, mismatched gutters, labels not baseline-aligned to their values.
anchors.recommendation: Introduce a column grid; align all block left-edges and label/value baselines; equalise gutters. Judge twice; keep the lower score.

anchors.band: mostly aligned, one or two items drift off the grid
anchors.critique: The layout mostly holds to a grid, but one or two elements drift — a heading indented a few px, or a control that doesn't share its neighbour's baseline.
anchors.evidence: Perceptual: predominant shared left-edge with 1-2 visible exceptions.
anchors.recommendation: Pull the stray elements back onto the shared edge/baseline; verify against a column overlay.

anchors.band: crisp shared edges and even gutters throughout
anchors.critique: Every block shares clean left/right edges and baselines; gutters are even and the eye tracks down a calm, ordered column.
anchors.evidence: Perceptual: consistent shared edges and baselines across cards, labels and controls.
anchors.recommendation: None material.

anchors.band: critical-error: body text illegibly small / over-set, or no heading-body distinction
anchors.critique: Body copy is set too small to read comfortably (or line length is unmanageable), and headings are indistinguishable from body — the type provides no reading structure.
anchors.evidence: type-scale-sprawl with body sizes below a legible floor; no size/weight gap between heading and body.
anchors.recommendation: Set a legible body size (>=16px web) with 1.4-1.6 line-height; establish a clear heading step; cap the ramp at ~6 distinct styles.

anchors.band: ramp sprawls (9+ distinct triples) but stays readable
anchors.critique: Text is readable, but the type ramp sprawls into nine or more distinct size/weight/line-height combinations, so the hierarchy feels undisciplined and slightly noisy.
anchors.evidence: type-scale-sprawl > 6 distinct (size, weight, line-height) triples.
anchors.recommendation: Consolidate to a modular scale of <=6 styles; map each style to a semantic role (display/heading/body/caption).

anchors.band: tight modular ramp, clear heading/body/caption
anchors.critique: A small, deliberate type ramp gives an obvious heading/body/caption split; body line-height sits in the comfortable 1.4-1.6 band.
anchors.evidence: <=6 distinct type triples; clear heading-to-body contrast.
anchors.recommendation: None material.

anchors.band: critical-error: any body text below 4.5:1 (WCAG AA fail)
anchors.critique: Body text fails WCAG AA contrast — light-grey copy on a white card drops below 4.5:1 and is hard to read; this is a hard-standard failure, not a taste call.
anchors.evidence: wcag-contrast / axe color-contrast: body text measured below 4.5:1.
anchors.recommendation: Darken body text (or lighten the background) until every text run clears 4.5:1 (>=3:1 for large text); verify with the contrast checker, not by eye.

anchors.band: large text passes but the grey palette is fragmented
anchors.critique: All text technically passes contrast, but the greys are fragmented into many near-duplicate values, so surfaces and borders feel muddy and inconsistent.
anchors.evidence: color-inventory-sprawl: multiple near-duplicate greys; no contrast failures.
anchors.recommendation: Consolidate greys to a small token ramp (e.g. 5-7 steps); tint them with a hint of the brand hue; use one accent sparingly.

anchors.band: all text clears AA, small consistent token palette
anchors.critique: Every text run clears WCAG AA, the palette is small and tokenised, and the accent colour is used sparingly for genuine emphasis — legible and harmonious.
anchors.evidence: No wcag-contrast findings; consolidated grey ramp; single restrained accent.
anchors.recommendation: None material; consider an AAA pass for body text if the audience needs it.

consistency.question: Same components, spacing and type across screens?

anchors.band: critical-error: a shared component renders differently across core screens
anchors.critique: The same component — a button or card — renders with different padding, radius or type on different core screens, so the product feels stitched from unrelated parts.
anchors.evidence: visual-regression > 5% baseline drift on a shared component; per-screen rule-count and type-triple-set diffs.
anchors.recommendation: Extract the divergent component to a single shared implementation with shared spacing/type/colour tokens; re-baseline.

anchors.band: minor drift in spacing/type between screens
anchors.critique: Patterns are recognisably the same across screens, but spacing or type drifts subtly between them, so the rhythm wobbles as you navigate.
anchors.evidence: visual-regression in the 5-15% band; small per-screen type-triple diffs.
anchors.recommendation: Unify the drifting spacing/type onto shared tokens; add a visual-regression baseline to hold it.

anchors.band: pixel-stable repeated patterns
anchors.critique: Repeated patterns are pixel-stable across screens; the same component looks identical everywhere, so navigation feels like one coherent product.
anchors.evidence: No visual regressions above threshold; matching rule-counts and type-triple sets across screens.
anchors.recommendation: None material.

empty-error-states.question: Quality of empty / loading / error / blank-render states?

anchors.band: critical-error: render crash or a blank screen where content is expected
anchors.critique: The screen rendered blank (or threw an uncaught error) where content was expected — the user hits a dead end with no explanation and no way forward.
anchors.evidence: pageError (uncaught exception) OR a near-blank screenshot where content was expected.
anchors.recommendation: Fix the render crash; then design an empty/error state that names what's missing and offers a next action.

anchors.band: functional but bare empty/error states (no guidance)
anchors.critique: Empty and error states render without crashing, but they are bare — a lone icon or a terse 'No data', with no explanation of what's missing or what to do next.
anchors.evidence: Screenshot shows an empty state with no supporting copy or recovery action; no pageError.
anchors.recommendation: Add a one-line explanation plus a primary next action (create/import/retry); make error messages human and recoverable.

anchors.band: informative, recoverable, on-brand empty/error states
anchors.critique: Empty and error states explain what's missing, offer a clear next action, and stay on-brand — the user always knows where they are and how to proceed.
anchors.evidence: No pageError; empty state carries explanatory copy + a primary action; errors are human and recoverable.
anchors.recommendation: None material.

affordance.question: Do controls signal that they act, and give feedback?

anchors.band: critical-error: the primary action is dead (no feedback on click)
anchors.critique: The primary action produces no observable effect when clicked — no navigation, DOM change, network call or feedback. It looks live but is dead, the worst affordance failure.
anchors.evidence: dead-control (effect:none) on the primary button; or click-error / non-actionable primary control.
anchors.recommendation: Wire the primary action and give immediate feedback (state change, spinner, toast); never ship a control that looks interactive but does nothing.

anchors.band: secondary controls are sub-target or lack focus signifiers
anchors.critique: The primary action works, but secondary controls fall below the 44px/48dp tap-target minimum or suppress the focus outline with no :focus-visible replacement, hurting touch and keyboard use.
anchors.evidence: tap-target < 44px on secondary controls; missing-focus-visible (outline suppressed, no :focus-visible rule); axe target-size/focus.
anchors.recommendation: Raise tap targets to >=44px/48dp; restore a visible focus ring via :focus-visible; ensure every interactive element signals interactivity (cursor/hover).

anchors.band: every control is affordant, >=44px, with a visible focus ring and feedback
anchors.critique: Every interactive element looks interactive, meets the tap-target minimum, shows a clear keyboard focus ring, and gives feedback on action — affordance is complete for mouse, touch and keyboard.
anchors.evidence: No dead-control/tap-target/missing-focus-visible findings; axe focus/target-size clean.
anchors.recommendation: None material.

motion.question: Is motion purposeful, smooth, and respectful?

anchors.band: critical-error: janky/blocking motion, or motion with no reduced-motion escape
anchors.critique: Animation blocks interaction or drops frames, and the page animates with no prefers-reduced-motion escape — actively harmful to users who need calm or are motion-sensitive.
anchors.evidence: reduced-motion: page animates but ships no prefers-reduced-motion rule; motion-duration far out of band / visibly janky.
anchors.recommendation: Add a prefers-reduced-motion:reduce rule that disables or shortens non-essential motion; remove blocking/janky animation from the interaction path.

anchors.band: durations out of band, or motion that doesn't aid comprehension
anchors.critique: Transitions fire but sit outside the ~200-500ms band (too slow or too abrupt) or decorate rather than clarify cause and effect, so motion adds latency without meaning.
anchors.evidence: motion-duration outside the 200-500ms band; transitions that don't map to a state change.
anchors.recommendation: Retune durations into the 200-500ms band; tie each transition to a real state change so motion explains cause and effect.

anchors.band: snappy in-band motion that clarifies state and respects reduced-motion
anchors.critique: Transitions are snappy and in-band, clarify what changed and why, and honour prefers-reduced-motion — motion is purposeful and respectful.
anchors.evidence: motion-duration within 200-500ms; prefers-reduced-motion rule present; no jank.
anchors.recommendation: None material.
